items.name: Toric complete-intersection p-adic weight–monodromy
items.statement: Theorem 5.6 states that for a smooth scheme-theoretic complete intersection Y over C_p in a projective smooth toric variety, H_HK^i(Y^an) is quasi-pure of weight i. The written rank-one argument applies to geometrically connected positive-dimensional Y; the dimension-zero case needs its elementary separate argument. If variety means integral over the algebraically closed base, connectedness is already implicit. For a reading allowing arbitrary disconnected smooth schemes, a componentwise argument remains G2. Remark 5.8 does not prove connectedness for arbitrary non-ample toric hypersurface cuts. This review does not refute the main weight–monodromy conclusion.

changes.before: For a morphism X→X' between log-smooth objects over an integral quasi-coherent log base S, étale locally on X,X',S there is a fine log structure M0→M_S and a log-smooth morphism over (S,M0) whose pullback is the given map. Finite presentation of chart monoids descends the map as well as the objects.
changes.after: For an arbitrary morphism f:X→X′ between log-smooth objects over an integral quasi-coherent log base S, étale locally on X, X′ and S there is a fine log structure M0→M_S and a morphism f0 between log-smooth objects over (S,M0) whose pullback is f.
